units.text: EXT. GLASS ORCHARD - TWILIGHT
An orchard of fruit trees blown from glass.
Trunks of smoky quartz, leaves of green crystal chiming faintly in a wind that smells of cold iron.
Each tree bears hundreds of apples, translucent, glowing from within like lanterns.
A winding path of white gravel leads to a stone well at the center.
ORSOLYA THANE (60s, gardener, tall, a gown the color of dry moss, silver hair braided to her waist) moves between the trunks with a pair of shears.
She trims nothing; she only touches the leaves, one by one, and listens as each rings a slightly different note.
At the well, she stops.
Rests a palm on its rim.
From within rises a pale breath of mist.
Another year. Another thousand apples. And not one of you has learned to fall.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: The leaves chime, as if in reply.
She takes an apple from a low branch, turns it in her fingers.
Inside, a small flame flickers, steady.
Patience. They said I was good at it.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: She sets the apple on the well's edge.
Another chime, this one deeper, from the roots.
She frowns.
Kneels.
Presses her ear to the quartz trunk.
A footstep on the gravel.
Not hers.
KAEDMON ASH (30s, a courier's cloak patched with ravens' feathers, boots soaked to the knee, face gaunt, eyes too bright) steps out between the trees.
He carries a leather satchel against his chest like an infant.
Gardener.
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: You are not expected.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Nor am I welcome. I know the ritual.
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: Then you know what the orchard does to those who bring iron.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: He opens his cloak.
A dagger, bare, at his belt.
I am not the one who needs the iron.
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: He reaches into the satchel and withdraws a seed the size of a child's fist, black and rough, ringed in thin gold wire.
The orchard's chimes fall silent.
Every leaf stills.
Orsolya rises slowly, gripping the shears.
Where did you get that?
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Where do you think?
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: From the one who swore never to plant it.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Promises rot faster than apples.
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: He kneels and presses the seed into the white gravel.
The ground shivers.
A hairline crack spreads across the path, and within it a green thread rises, fast, thickening.
Orsolya lunges.
Kaedmon blocks her with his arm; they struggle, her shears tearing his cloak, his dagger skimming her sleeve, until she shoves him against a trunk and the glass sings out in a long, frantic scream.
You will kill us all!
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: I will wake us.
units.name: KAEDMON

units.text: The root bursts from the earth, black, glittering, enormous, tearing the well in two.
Apples fall.

Hundreds, thousands, a rain of light, shattering on the gravel, each one releasing its tiny flame, and the orchard ignites, tree after tree, glowing gold and white, until the whole sky is fire and glass.
